headline: 7-3-1 on 11 value plays, +$31.95
paragraphs: 11 games finished in Week 11. It found a playable edge in 7 of them and left the other 4 alone. Those plays went 7-3-1, worth +$31.95 at $10 a play (29.0% on the $110 at risk).

By market, spreads went 3-2-1, totals went 3-0 and moneylines went 1-1. The best of them was Louisiana -10.5 in Louisiana at UL Monroe, a 8.3-point disagreement with the market that finished Louisiana 42, UL Monroe 21. The one that stung was Houston -9.5 in Houston at Colorado, a 4.9-point disagreement with the market that finished Colorado 42, Houston 32.

Season to date the model has made 453 value plays and gone 194-246-13, -$554.09 on flat $10 bets (-12.2%). It expected to win 60% of those and won 44%. On line movement, 5 of the 16 published picks whose numbers moved closed worse than the site posted them, so the market came our way 31% of the time. Sample is getting real enough to argue with, though a model that beats closing lines is rarer than one that beats a few hundred results.
